judge: Opus 5.5 (fresh adversarial reviewer agent, no prior scores)
rubric: height vs cliff, edge seams, style vs beodeul cliffs, front-elevation look, 1x readability

majors: Foot cell (last 16 rows) is a hard-edged rectangle of smooth dirt, full piece width with straight vertical sides against grass, wider than the native ragged-edged track (probe-1x rows 144-159 cols 16-47; sol32/terra32 crops: rectangular block overhanging the track); texture is sparser/smoother than the speckled native track, so the toe reads as a pasted patch, not the track continuing.

Crest/toe do not join the track in the probe: full grass rows between the upper track end and the crest (probe-1x rows 126-127) and between the foot cell and the lower track (rows 160-161); the piece gives the track autotile nothing to connect to.
minors: Ramp fill (138,116,92 dominant) with long 1px vertical streaks is a lower-density, more regular texture than the clustered native cliff/track speckle.
Corner grass tufts at the crest are 2-3px squares, smaller than the native 4px jagged grass lip, so the cut's top corners look nibbled.
At rise 1 the missing slope cue matters less (reads as a notch), but the toe/crest seams remain.

majors: Edge seam with paved road: the foot cell and the cut are unframed cobble/stone with straight sides against grass, while the beodeul road has a light-grey curb frame; in probe-3x and the sol31/sol32 stairs crops the upper road's bottom curb line runs right across the crest and the lower road's top curb crosses below the foot cell, so the road visibly ends in a curb on both sides of the flight and the stairs read as a separate pasted block.
minors: Top tread highlight row sits directly under the road curb line, giving a doubled light line at the crest.
Steps are 8px each (2 per row of rise); in h1 the treads are only ~3px and read as stripes at 1x, though still legible as steps.
Side walls are thin (3-4px) jagged dirt strips, thinner than the native cliff end caps.
Height matches the native face rows exactly; treads read clearly as a way up at 1x.

majors: Stacked flights inherit the single-piece seams: the upper flight's foot cell on the one-row strip is a straight-edged rectangle (dirt for ramps, unframed cobble for stairs) against grass, so the landing reads as a pasted patch rather than the track/road crossing the terrace (probe2-3x middle x 630-955, right x 1200-1530, rows ~383-485).
Ramp stacks have no slope cue on either flight (same flat vertical-streak fill), so the composition reads as two slots with a patch between rather than a climbing path.
minors: Flights align horizontally and the walls stop cleanly at the landing; height split (floor(total/2) lower) is correct in both probe2 cases.
Right stack (1+strip+2): lower 1-row stair flight is compressed to two thin treads.

summary: Heights are correct for all 16 pieces (rise rows match the native face rows; foot lands on the lower ground) and the stairs read clearly as a way up at 1x. All fail on joins: ramps have rectangular smooth foot cells wider than the ragged native track and grass gaps at crest/toe in the probe, and ramps of rise 2-4 have no slope cue (flat vertical-streak panel reads as a slot/door). Stairs fail because the unframed stone/cobble cut and foot meet the curb-framed road with a curb line across crest and toe, so the flight looks like a separate block. Stacked flights inherit these seams.
